:::{#exm-repetition-code}
#### Sending each bit three times

To send one bit over the
[binary symmetric channel](#def-binary-symmetric-channel)
with $\epsilon = 0.1$,
send it three times and decode by majority vote.
This is a $(2, 3)$ [channel code](#def-channel-code), with rate $R = 1/3$.
The decoder is wrong when two or three of the copies are flipped,
which happens with probability

$$
\begin{aligned}
\lambda^{(3)}
&= 3 \epsilon^2 (1 - \epsilon) + \epsilon^3 \\
&= 3 (0.01)(0.9) + 0.001 \\
&= 0.028,
\end{aligned}
$$

down from $0.1$ for sending the bit once.
Repeating more often lowers the error further,
but the rate falls toward $0$ as it does.
@mackay2003information [chapter 1] works through this code.

:::
